statement: For every nonempty exact shell, \(1\le D\le C\le e^\eta\); because the supports are finite, either \((C,D)=(1,1)\) or \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\). Conversely, for every \(d\ge4\) and every pair \(1<D\le C<e^\eta\), there is a finite public experiment with bounded features and nonsingular logging covariance for which \(\mathcal M(d,C,D,\eta)\ne\varnothing\); the pair \((1,1)\) is also realizable. Thus the feasible index region when the public experiment may vary is exactly \(\{(1,1)\}\cup\{(C,D):1<D\le C<e^\eta\}\). Feasibility for a fixed public experiment can be strictly smaller: canonical tabular features force \(D=C\), whereas shared features realize off-diagonal pairs \(D<C\). This theorem answers the feasibility part of the question; it does not assert a minimax lower frontier outside the proved local hard regime.
proof_tex:
Write
\[
w_x(a)=\frac{e^{\eta r_\theta(x,a)}}{\sum_b\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(b\mid x)e^{\eta r_\theta(x,b)}}.
\]
For every \(x\), \(\mathbb E_{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid x)}w_x(A)=1\), so its essential supremum is at least one and \(C\ge1\). Since \(0\le r_\theta\le1\), the numerator is at most \(e^\eta\) and the denominator is at least one, giving \(C\le e^\eta\). If equality held at a supported cell, that cell would have reward one and the denominator would have to equal one. Its strictly positive reference mass would then make the denominator strictly larger than one, a contradiction. Hence \(C<e^\eta\) whenever \(C>1\).

The inequality \(w_x(a)\le C\) implies
\[
\Lambda_P^\star\preceq C\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}},
\]
so \(D\le C\). To obtain the lower inequality, suppose first that \(\theta\ne0\). At a fixed context let \(R=r_\theta(x,A)\) under the reference action law and let \(R'\) be an independent copy. Exponential tilting gives
\[
\mathbb E_{\pi_P^\star}R^2-\mathbb E_{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}R^2
=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}(R^2,e^{\eta R})}{\mathbb E_{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}e^{\eta R}},
\]
and
\[
2\operatorname{Cov}(R^2,e^{\eta R})
=\mathbb E[(R^2-R'^2)(e^{\eta R}-e^{\eta R'})]\ge0,
\]
because both functions are increasing on \([0,1]\). Averaging over contexts yields
\[
\theta^\top\Lambda_P^\star\theta\ge\theta^\top\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\theta>0.
\]
The Rayleigh quotient characterization gives \(D\ge1\). If \(\theta=0\), every reward is zero, the two policies and covariances coincide, and again \(D=1\).

If \(D=1\), then \(\Lambda_P^\star\preceq\Lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\). The preceding nonnegative quadratic difference in the direction \(\theta\) must be zero. Every contextwise covariance in its integral is nonnegative, so it is zero for \(\rho\)-almost every context. The independent-copy display and strict monotonicity of \(r\mapsto r^2\) and \(r\mapsto e^{\eta r}\) on \([0,1]\) show that the reward is constant on the reference support at each such context. The Gibbs tilt is then trivial, so \(\pi_P^\star=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) and \(C=1\). Conversely, \(C=1\) implies \(D=1\) by the mean-one likelihood-ratio argument in \(\text{thm:zero-risk-boundary}\). This proves the necessary region.

For sufficiency, fix an orthonormal basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}\) and two actions \(\{1,0\}\). For \(1<K<e^\eta\), put
\[
q_K=\frac{e^\eta/K-1}{e^\eta-1}\in(0,1).
\]
Take \(\theta=\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}e_j\). At a context \(x_C\), let the action-one feature be \(e_0\), the action-zero feature be zero, and give action one reference probability \(q_C\). At contexts \(x_j\), \(1\le j\le d-1\), use the analogous pair \(e_j,0\) and reference probability \(q_D\). At each such context the rewards are one and zero, the Gibbs likelihood ratio of action one is respectively \(C\) or \(D\), and the other ratio is respectively \(C/e^\eta\) or \(D/e^\eta\).

When \(C>D\), add a context \(x_A\) at which both actions have feature \(e_0\), and set its context mass relative to that of \(x_C\) equal to
\[
A=\frac{q_C(C-D)}{D-1}.
\]
Both actions then have reward one and the Gibbs policy equals the reference policy at \(x_A\). If \(C=D\), omit \(x_A\). Give every displayed context a positive raw mass and normalize while preserving the ratio \(A\) between the two \(e_0\) contexts. In direction \(e_0\), the target-to-logging covariance ratio is
\[
\frac{q_CC+A}{q_C+A}=D.
\]
In every direction \(e_j\), \(j\ge1\), it is also \(D\). Hence the logging covariance is positive definite and the generalized-eigenvalue index is exactly \(D\), while the pointwise index is exactly \(C\). This realizes every interior pair. For \((C,D)=(1,1)\), take \(d\) positive-mass contexts, one action, features \(e_j\), and \(\theta=0\).

Finally, canonical features make both covariance matrices diagonal with coordinatewise ratios equal to the policy likelihood ratios, forcing \(D=C\). The construction above uses the same feature direction \(e_0\) at \(x_C\) and \(x_A\) and realizes \(D<C\), so feasibility for a fixed public experiment genuinely depends on its feature design. The construction proves feasibility but supplies no minimax lower family outside the already proved local hard region, which is why the conclusion is deliberately partial.
justification: Mean-one Gibbs likelihood ratios, covariance ordering, and an explicit shared-feature construction characterize the varying-design feasible index set.
gap: The theorem resolves feasibility only and deliberately does not claim minimax lower frontiers outside the local hard region.
consumer: It distinguishes intrinsically impossible index pairs from pairs that are realizable by some public feature design, while warning that a fixed experiment may be more restrictive.
